title: Sequenced output guarantees and SDKs interop experiments
summary: Quick working doc exploring a lightweight contract for sequenced partial outputs, atomic checkpoints for interleaved tool calls, and an ergonomic SDK surface that is resilient to network reordering and client restarts. Focus is on developer mental model, telemetry hooks, and acceptance criteria for a minimal first pass experiment.
goals: Define a minimal sequencing contract for progressive responses that supports: ordered user-visible tokens, interleaved tool-call frames, and checkpointing for resume/replay.
Design SDK primitives that make it easy to: (a) attach per-frame assertions, (b) resume a session after a dropped connection, and (c) synthesize tool results with deterministic reconciliation.

Produce an experiment plan that can run against the hosted-api streaming endpoint with two client SDK implementations (node + python) and a small corpus of prompts that exercise tool fanout and partial JSON outputs.
non_goals: Full production security review (out of scope for the experiment).
Complete API surface parity with existing callback-heavy SDKs — aim is a constrained ergonomic subset.
Building server-side fallback orchestration for multi-region hedging — only client-visible behavior is spec'd.
user_stories: As a frontend engineer, I want the SDK to surface stable checkpoints so I can show partial results and let users continue after a network blip without misordered snippets.

As an integrations engineer, I want tool-call frames to be deterministically re-playable so downstream systems can idempotently apply results even if the same tool is invoked multiple times during retries.
As an SRE, I want lightweight telemetry hooks (frame ids, latency per-frame, drop/retry counters) so we can correlate regressions to model variants and client SDK versions.
requirements: Streaming wire-layer includes monotonically-increasing frame index (uint32) and optional checkpoint_id string.
Three high-level frame types: TEXT_CHUNK, TOOL_EVENT, CHECKPOINT. Clients must preserve order by frame index; the server guarantees index monotonicity per session.
CHECKPOINT frames capture (a) visible output fingerprint (sha256 of last N chars), (b) minimal KV of tool-call outcomes referenced by stable ids, and (c) model version tag.
SDK must expose: beginSession(), onFrame(cb), requestResume(checkpoint_id), and synthesizeLocalToolResult(tool_id, result) to allow client-driven reconciliation during offline/edge cases.
Tool events carry stable invocation ids and an explicit idempotency token; SDKs should auto-generate tokens unless provided.
A simple deterministic replay mode: client can request frames since checkpoint X and the server will return a canonical tail; server must include a small replay-proof signature for the checkpoint.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment runs 1000 short sessions (<= 200 tokens) with simulated 10% packet loss and 5% reordering; Node and Python SDKs correctly reconstruct ordered text and tool results for >= 98% of sessions.
Tool-call idempotency validated: repeated delivery of the same tool invocation id results in at most one recorded side effect in the test harness.
Latency overhead of adding frame indices and checkpoint metadata is < 1% p50 token latency in our synthetic perf harness for small models (baseline: current streaming endpoint).
Telemetry emitted for every frame (frame_index, frame_type, latency_ms); traces are queryable in Console in under 60s for the experiment dataset.
compatibility_and_migration_notes: Existing clients that ignore unknown fields should continue to work; frame_index will be appended to existing streaming frames as a top-level attribute.
Server will support a compatibility header X-Seq-Protocol: v1|opt-in for first month, then opt-out as default to minimize disruption.
observability_plan: Emit per-frame telemetry: {session_id, frame_index, frame_type, model_version, ttf_ms}.
Add a Console view to aggregate 'checkpoint health' (percent of sessions successfully resumed without divergence).
Flag sessions with checksum mismatches and surface probable root cause (reordering vs model-drift).
experiment_plan: Phase 0: Local prototype with a toy server that injects reordering and loss; validate SDK logic and deterministic replay signature format.
Phase 1: Canary on hosted-api test cluster for internal SDK clients only (1% of internal usage).
Phase 2: Run 1k synthetic sessions from different regions; collect success/failure metrics and telemetry.
Phase 3: Iterate on ergonomics (callback vs async iterator) based on developer feedback, then open to beta customers.
open_questions: How large should the checkpoint fingerprint window be? tradeoff: resume reliability vs metadata size.
Do we require server-signed checkpoint proofs (HMAC) on v1 or can rely on best-effort canonical tail for experiment?
Should SDKs automatically coalesce adjacent TEXT_CHUNK frames for display, or leave that to application logic? (convenience vs transparency)
What is the UX for partial JSON outputs that are emitted incrementally and later corrected by the model? how to present to users?
notes_to_self: Talk to infra about adding a lightweight hmac key for checkpoints in the test cluster.
Schedule 30m sync with SDK leads (Priya/Miguel) next week to try async iterator API draft.
Add a small evaluation prompt set: interleaved tool calls (lookup, calculator), partial JSON streaming, and mid-stream corrections.
Keep experiment surface intentionally small: focus on developer experience and measurable metrics, not full productization.
